summary:
Re-verified iteration-7 fix claims on /visualiser at 1440x900 using two synthetic house images (/tmp/test_house.jpg — 800x600 with ~40px bare margins around a boxy dark frame, /tmp/test_house_narrow.jpg — same layout but ~20px bare margins). Also ran the node harness /app/scripts/test_wall_detect.mjs which passes 7/7 (F: door 91%, frames 22%/18%; G trap: pieceWall 0%, frame 22%, door 94%; E both walls 100%). The node harness works because it renders at 400x300; the browser renders these images through detectWallMask at 800x600 and results are very different.

WALLS (standard 800x600) — PASS and better than iteration-6: main-wall-left 100%, main-between 98%, right-wall top 98%, right-wall bottom 100%, right-wall bare left strip 100%, right-wall bare right strip 88%, sky/ground/door/glass/frame/downpipe all 0%, soft-alpha pixels 0. Painting Forest green in isolation shifts both wall faces to (64,90,77)/(62,89,74) and leaves sky/ground/door/glass/frame unchanged. Edges are crisp.

WOODWORK (standard 800x600) — CRITICAL REGRESSION: after Detect Woodwork on a freshly-loaded page (no walls detect prior, no residual mask), the brush overlay shows ONLY the glass pane (glass 100%) and 0% on the door, 0% on all four frame strips, 0% on walls/sky/ground/downpipe. Painting Anthracite (#3D3D3D) then Generate leaves the door RGB unchanged from source ((25,32,60) -> (25,32,60)) AND the frame RGB unchanged ((45,42,38) -> (45,41,38)) — while the GLASS is tinted ((180,195,210) -> (166,180,193)). This is WORSE than iteration-6: door dropped from 85% -> 0% coverage, and the enclosed-pick tie-break claim ("keep the thin ring, drop the solid pane") is doing the opposite here (glass is kept, frame + door are dropped entirely). Fix #1 (384px woodwork analysis) and Fix #2 (fill-ratio tie-break for enclosed picks) do NOT hold in the browser on 800x600.

NARROW WALLS variant — FAIL: on /tmp/test_house_narrow.jpg (right-wall bare margins ~20px around a large window), auto-detect walls covers the main wall 82% but the four bare-margin strips read 0% (left 0%, right 0%, top 66% only because that is the fatter top band above the window, bot 0%). The glass reads 100% coverage, i.e. the walls mask INCORRECTLY includes the glass pane. Fix #3 (35-seed grid + fx 0.96 / fy 0.74) does not seed the 20px bare strips and the enclosed-openings union pulls in the glass. Downstream: painting the walls with green would tint the glass pane.

MOBILE 390x844 — NOT REACHED: due to the HIGH desktop regressions above I did not spend cycles on mobile. Iteration-6 confirmed no horizontal overflow at 390x844 and no code that affects layout was touched in this iteration; the mobile detector will exhibit the SAME woodwork glass-only pick because it is the algorithm not the layout.

REGRESSIONS — homepage renders (title 'TMN Decorating & Maintenance | Painter & Decorator Plymouth', hero + CTA visible), admin@tmndecorating.co.uk / TMN-Admin-2026! -> /admin OK. Customer login was tested in the same browser context after admin login and redirected to /admin because the admin cookie survived my /logout attempt (env has no /logout route to hit directly) — this is a test-harness artefact, not a product bug (iteration-6 already confirmed customer -> /account when tested from a fresh context). Console noise limited to expected /api/auth/me 401.

ui_bugs.issue: Woodwork auto-detect now picks ONLY the glass pane (glass 100% overlay) and MISSES the door completely (door 0%, down from 85% in iteration-6) and all four window-frame strips (frame_top/bot/left/right all 0%). After painting anthracite the door RGB is unchanged from source ((25,32,60)->(25,32,60)) and the frame RGB is unchanged ((45,42,38)->(45,41,38)), while the glass is tinted ((180,195,210)->(166,180,193)). The fill-ratio tie-break claim in Fix #2 fails in the browser at 800x600 — the enclosed-pick drop keeps the glass and drops the frame + door. Increasing woodwork analysis width to 384px (Fix #1) has NOT recovered the frame ring; and it has now cost us the door too, indicating the wall-Lab gate or the enclosed-pick drop is now rejecting the door pick at 384px scaling.

When the right-return wall's bare margin around the window is ~20px, the walls auto-detect misses ALL bare strips (left 0%, right 0%, top-only 66% covered because top strip is fatter, bottom 0%) and instead the glass pane reads 100% coverage — the walls mask incorrectly includes the glass. Fix #3 (35-seed grid + fx 0.96 / fy 0.74) does not seed the 20px bare wall and the enclosed-openings union is unioning the glass into the wall mask. Painting walls would tint the glass.

node_harness.notes: F frame1 22%, frame2 18%, door 91%; G trap pieceWall 0%, frame 22%, door 94%; E two-walls A 100% B 100%. Node uses W=400 H=300; browser renders these test images at 800x600.

woodwork_desktop_standard.verdict: FAIL (regression) — glass tinted, door + frame untouched

walls_narrow_variant.verdict: FAIL — bare strips missed, glass included

regressions.customer_login: not re-tested from fresh context this iteration; iteration-6 confirmed -> /account

action_items: WOODWORK: the 384px woodwork analysis + fill-ratio tie-break combination is worse than iteration-6 on this 800x600 image. On a fresh page with only a woodwork detect run, the overlay is JUST the glass pane at 100% and door/frames are 0%. Painting anthracite tints the glass and leaves door + frame unchanged. Please instrument detectWallMask so we can see which picks fire, and check whether at 384px the door pick is now being rejected by the wall-Lab gate (source door is (25,32,60), main wall is (250,248,244) — no way the door reads as wall) or by the enclosed-pick drop against the glass bbox.

WOODWORK: the fill-ratio tie-break appears to be selecting the SOLID glass over the RING frame. Verify the two picks are actually reaching the tie-break with equal bboxes — if the frame pick is being dropped upstream (e.g. because the flood-fill at 384px cannot cross the 6-8px frame from outside and picks up only the interior glass), no tie-break can save it. Consider seeding the woodwork flood from the darkest edge pixels of any enclosed dark-vs-bright bbox rather than from the interior.

WALLS narrow variant: 20px bare strips still missed and glass 100% included. The enclosed-openings union is pulling the glass into the wall mask when the wall around a window is thin. Please gate the enclosed-hole fill on 'was this hole surrounded on all four sides by wall-coloured pixels within N px' — 20px is likely below whatever N is currently.

Test harness gap: node harness renders at W=400 H=300 and passes 7/7, browser renders these synthetic images at 800x600 and both features fail. Consider updating /app/scripts/test_wall_detect.mjs to also cover W=800 H=600 so this regression would have been caught before shipping.
critical_code_review_comments: detectWallMask WALLS branch is now excellent on the standard 800x600 image (both faces covered, crisp edges, 0 partial-alpha, no bleed onto sky/door/glass/frame/downpipe/ground) — the walls-union-with-sticksDownOnly rejection is doing its job.

detectWallMask WOODWORK branch has regressed on 800x600: the door (a solid dark blob that worked fine in iteration-6 at 85%) now reads 0% coverage. Combined with the frame still at 0% and the glass now at 100%, this suggests the 384px branch + new tie-break is systematically preferring the largest enclosed dark-vs-bright pick and rejecting everything else. Recommend a regression case in the node harness at W=800 H=600 with the iteration-6 synthetic to lock down door detection.

The enclosed-openings union used by walls is over-eager on thin-return-wall images: a glass pane with only 20px of wall around it is treated as 'wall with a hole', not 'wall with a window' — same bug that also lets woodwork mis-pick the glass. Consider a single shared 'is this a window' classifier that both branches trust.

success_rate.frontend: walls (standard): PASS; walls (narrow): FAIL; woodwork (standard): CRITICAL FAIL — regressed vs iteration-6

context_for_next_testing_agent: The node harness at /app/scripts/test_wall_detect.mjs still passes 7/7 at W=400 H=300 but the real browser algorithm at 800x600 has two open bugs. WOODWORK: door + frame both drop to 0% coverage on the standard synthetic image, glass rises to 100% and gets tinted when anthracite is applied — this is WORSE than iteration-6 (which at least had the door at 85%). WALLS: narrow-margin variant (bare strips ~20px) has 0% on bare strips and 100% on glass, so painting walls would tint the glass. WALLS on standard image is PASS. Reproduce: python3 gen /tmp/test_house.jpg per iteration-6 recipe, upload, click WOODWORK layer, click Detect, sample brush canvas alpha — you'll see only the glass rectangle painted. Then Anthracite -> Generate -> compare AFTER RGB at (300,350)=door, (730,224)=frame_top, (730,295)=glass. Add a W=800 H=600 regression to the node harness so future fixes cannot silently regress.
rca_of_the_issue: The node harness renders at 400x300 and detectWallMask internally scales to 256px walls / 384px woodwork; at this scale the woodwork flood-fill successfully crosses a 6-8px frame boundary and the fill-ratio tie-break picks the ring over the pane. In the browser these same synthetic images arrive at 800x600 and the internal scaling puts them close to native size; the woodwork flood-fill at 384px on a 800x600 source fails to cross the frame (probably because localDiff=18 rejects the light-vs-dark step at native contrast) so the ONLY dark-vs-bright pick the woodwork branch sees on this image is the enclosed glass, and it happily paints that. Meanwhile the door — which is far darker than the wall — should still be a slam-dunk pick but is now also 0% at 800x600, so either the wall-Lab gate is rejecting it (unlikely, huge Lab distance) or an unrelated code path (perhaps the enclosed-pick drop counting the door as 'enclosed inside the wall bbox' because the wall bbox is now almost the whole photo after the 0.85 overflow cap widened) is dropping the door. That would also explain why iteration-6 had door 85% (overflow cap 0.72 discarded the huge wall pick, so the enclosed-drop had no wall bbox to compare against) and iteration-7 has door 0% (overflow cap 0.85 keeps the wall, wall bbox encloses the door, door is dropped as 'enclosed').
